subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in Telegram unauthorized-group-sender reply, and what rate-limit, privacy, admin-contact, and default-silent semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes behavior at a Telegram authorization-denial boundary and may expose raw user IDs or amplify group messages, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram-plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding notice with per-sender cooldown, topic-safe delivery, admin-contact configuration, and documented raw-ID handling.

options.title: Fold Into Operator Audit Only
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and route visibility through broader denied-inbound audit or owner-notification work instead of replying in the group.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and document `groupAllowFrom`, logs, and manual ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram-plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding notice with per-sender cooldown, topic-safe delivery, admin-contact configuration, and documented raw-ID handling.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent current-main signal across Telegram ingress, docs, and authorization-adjacent maintenance.
